extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and readers interested in academic publishing and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reported practice around journal policies forbidding prior or simultaneous publication and the editorial response when duplicate/identical papers are discovered. Focused on journal submission conditions and retraction actions for duplicated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement / no prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: “One of the conditions of submission of a paper for publication in Thai Journal of Mathematics that their work is original and has not been previously published...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals require submissions to be original and not previously published; violation (publication of identical prior work) is grounds for retraction. The retraction note cites the identical earlier paper as the reason for retracting the later article.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous submission / not under consideration elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: “…nor is it before another journal for consideration.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must not submit the same manuscript to more than one journal at the same time. This clause is commonly part of submission conditions and aims to prevent duplicate/overlapping review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate/identical publication triggers retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction note: “This article has been retracted at the request of the Editor-in-Chief because it is identical with a paper that had been already appeared in J. Appl. Math. Informatics Vol. 28(2010) No. 3-4, pp. 923-929...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a published article is found to be essentially identical to a previously published paper, journals may issue a retraction citing the prior publication and the editor's request. Retraction notices typically identify the earlier work and state the duplication as the rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility to detect duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: “Thai Journal of Mathematics would like to apologize readers that this was not detected during the submission process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals are expected to screen submissions for prior publication/duplication (e.g., via editorial checks or plagiarism detection). If duplication is missed, journals may acknowledge editorial oversight and retract the paper when duplication is discovered post-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify/contact the author when duplication discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction Watch: “We’ve also emailed the author, Amnuay Kananthai, who works at Chiang Mai University in Thailand.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a potential duplicate is reported or discovered, best practice includes contacting the author for explanation and to inform them of the investigation and any corrective action (retraction, correction). Public reporting (e.g., retraction notices) often follows editorial decision and author contact.
